name: Icon
purpose: Communicates meaning, action, or status through a recognizable visual symbol. Always supplemental to text — never the sole conveyor of information without a tooltip or label.
neverUseFor: Decorative illustration — use an Illustration component instead
Brand logomarks — use Image or dedicated Logo component
Animated icons — Tabler outline icons are static; wrap in a motion component if animation is needed

tablerOfficialStroke.note: Tabler default. Goes on the root <svg> ONLY — never on <path> children. Configurable via CSS.

helixStrokeOverride.note: Helix DS design decision. Always pass stroke={1.5} at usage site: <IconPlus size={16} stroke={1.5} />. Never hardcode — use the prop.

mustFollow: Only <path> elements inside SVG — no <circle>, <rect>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polygon>, <polyline>, <g>. Convert everything to path.
stroke-width goes on root <svg> only — never on child <path> elements
fill=none on outline icons — stroke only, never filled areas
stroke=currentColor on root <svg> — never hardcode a color
No closing Z on outline icon paths (Tabler removes it via optimizer)
Optical weight must match Tabler icons at 24px with stroke-width=2
Minimum path detail: legible at 16×16px (smallest Helix usage size)
Naming in Figma: PascalCase, no prefix — 'HeartCustom' (matching Tabler's bare-name convention)
SVG file metadata comment: tags, category (one of the 41 official), version, unicode
Every outline icon may optionally have a matching filled variant in icons/filled/
mustNot: Use stroke-width on <path> elements — only on root <svg>
Add fills or gradients to outline icons
Use sharp corners (linecap: butt, linejoin: miter) — always round
Include Z/z close-path on outline icon paths
Include title or desc SVG elements — accessibility is the usage site's responsibility
Use more than 3 path elements — simpler is better; complex icons suggest wrong category
referenceIcons: IconPlus — simplest form: 2 paths (vertical + horizontal line)
IconAlertCircle — 3 paths: circle arc + exclamation body + dot (h.01 trick with round linecap)
IconSearch — 2 paths: circle arc + handle line

sizes.system: fixed values — never scale with CSS font-size

values.12: xs contexts — dense UI, inline badges
values.16: default — button slots, form elements, inline text
values.20: medium emphasis — card headers, section labels
values.24: large — native icon size, icon-only buttons, empty states

sizes.note: Icon components always render at the size passed via the size prop. The Figma component is 24×24 (native grid); resize the instance at usage site.

colorRules.principle: Icons use their own icon/* semantic tokens, set explicitly — never inherited from a text/* token, even when the resolved color happens to match
colorRules.standalone: Use icon/neutral-dark, icon/neutral-light, or icon/neutral-lightest — never text/* tokens, never primitives
colorRules.forbidden: Never hardcode hex values. Never reference a text/* token for icon color. Never use primitive color scales directly.

anatomy.description: SVG element with viewBox='0 0 24 24'. Never add a wrapper div.

anatomy.element: path (or g > path for compound icons)
anatomy.description: The drawn artwork. stroke=currentColor, fill=none, stroke-width=1.5.

props.name: stroke
props.description: Stroke width applied to the icon path.

props.name: color
props.description: Icon stroke color. Prefer inherited currentColor.

props.name: decorative
props.description: Marks the icon as decorative when a visible label already exists.

figma.layout: Flat grid — COMPONENT nodes directly on page, no row frames

a11y.aria: aria-hidden='true' when accompanied by a visible label. aria-label='Description' when icon-only.
a11y.note: The icon component itself renders aria-hidden. Accessibility is the responsibility of the usage site.

3. Export SVG — extract the path d= attribute
6. Run icons-to-figma skill Step 2–4 for the new icon
7. Verify: renders clearly at 16×16, stroke weight matches IconPlus at same size
